problem: Embodied AI increasingly trains on synthetic 3D scene datasets. Prior work treats these datasets as black boxes, and there has been no systematic study of dataset scale (number of scenes, navigable area) versus realism (visual fidelity, real-world object statistics) for generalizing to real scanned homes. Existing options are also flawed: synthetic sets are single-room (iTHOR), few in scenes (RoboTHOR, ReplicaCAD), incomplete or interpenetrating (3D-FRONT), or procedurally generated (ProcTHOR), and scans (HM3D, MP3D) are noisy, have holes and cannot be edited.
motivation: Procedural generation (ProcTHOR-10K) makes near-infinite scene counts possible, but whether that scale actually helps agents transfer to real-world scans had not been tested in a focused way. Only 216 of HM3D's 1000 scans are semantically annotated, and scans cannot support object rearrangement. High-quality, compositional, human-authored synthetic scenes could therefore be valuable if realism matters more than raw scale.
key_idea: Build HSSD-200, 211 human-authored, realistic, densely annotated synthetic houses. Then train identical ObjectNav agents on HSSD and on ProcTHOR, including scale-matched subsets, to show that scene realism, not scene count, limits zero-shot transfer to real-world scans.
insight:
Scale saturates quickly and realism is the bottleneck. In the scale-matched comparison (Fig. 6), ProcTHOR subsets were chosen to match HSSD's navigable-area distribution. HSSD-122 beats ProcTHOR-122 on HM3DSem val by 19.15 vs 9.33 SR and 7.71 vs 3.47 SPL. Going from ProcTHOR-122 to ProcTHOR-10K, about 80x more scenes, only raises SR from 9.33 to 12.53, still below HSSD-60 (17.4). HSSD is also measurably closer to real scans on every realism axis the paper checks:
- FID to HM3D: 65.2 vs 88.5.
- Co-occurrence cluster Jaccard with HM3D: 0.40 vs 0.14.
- Instances per scene: 329.7 vs 74.7.
- Per-scene navigable area and episode geodesic-distance distributions: ProcTHOR has many easy, short episodes.
Fine-tuning on HM3DSem erases most of the gap: all pretrained agents land at 47.85–48.48 SR, with HSSD-122 keeping a small SPL lead (23.10 vs 21.80). The authors argue the zero-shot regime is the one that reflects deployment to unseen environments. HSSD-trained agents transfer poorly to THOR scenes (27.5 SR on iTHOR, 9.57 on ProcTHOR), so the benefit is specifically alignment with real scans.
method: HSSD-200 dataset: 211 houses from the Floorplanner web interior-design tool, mostly realtor re-creations of real homes. Contains 18,656 unique artist-made objects (often matching real brands) across 466 categories and 53.2K m² of navigable area (252.2 m² per scene). Split train/val/test 60/20/20.

Object extraction and decomposition: each scene glTF is split into architecture and deduplicated object assets. 1,791 multi-object models were flagged, and 1,662 were segmented into 11,153 parts using connected components plus manual painting. Duplicate instances are aligned with oriented bounding boxes and one ICP iteration, and 2,883 models were manually aligned to a consistent up/front orientation.

Semantic categorization: objects are labeled with WordNetCo, WordNet augmented with common-object synsets. Labels were initialized from Floorplanner tags and refined by annotators, with extra attributes for the room an object is found in and its attachment side.

Asset compression and Habitat porting: quadric mesh simplification (error 1e-3), textures capped at 256 px and Basis supercompression give a 12.4x on-disk reduction. ProcTHOR, iTHOR and RoboTHOR were ported to Habitat the same way, giving roughly an order of magnitude higher FPS than AI2-THOR (e.g. 58,947 vs 8,599 FPS on 8 GPUs for ProcTHOR-S).

Realism and complexity analysis: FID/KID of Habitat renders against HM3D, Gibson and MP3D images. Object co-occurrence over 28 shared categories (centroids within 1 m) is compared with Spearman ρ and with the Jaccard index over hierarchical clusters (threshold 0.8, Hungarian matching). Also navigable area, navigation complexity and clutter.

ObjectNav agent (EmbCLIP-style): frozen CLIP ResNet-50 encodes 224x224 RGB into a 2048-d feature. Goal category, GPS+compass and previous action get 32-d embeddings, which feed a 2-layer LSTM and a linear action head. Trained with DD-PPO + VER on 4 A40 GPUs with 24 workers per GPU until convergence (~200M steps); the best-val-SPL checkpoint is kept and results are averaged over 3 runs.

Scale-vs-realism protocol: 1K episodes per scene for 6 goal categories, generated via viewpoint sampling with a frame-coverage ≥0.1% filter. Agents trained on iTHOR, ProcTHOR-10K, HSSD-122, MP3D and HM3DSem are evaluated on every dataset's val set. Scale-matched ProcTHOR-60/122 subsets and HSSD-60 are added, plus fine-tuning on HM3DSem.

setting.backbone: Frozen CLIP ResNet-50 visual encoder + 2-layer LSTM policy trained from scratch with DD-PPO/VER (end-to-end RL)
setting.training_data: HSSD-122 train scenes with 1K episodes each (122K episodes), trained to convergence (~200M steps). Comparison agents: iTHOR (64 scenes, 128K episodes), ProcTHOR-10K (10M episodes), ProcTHOR-60/122 subsets, MP3D (56 scenes, 925K), HM3DSem (145 scenes, 7.25M). Fine-tuned variants are further trained on HM3DSem train.
setting.observation: egocentric RGB 224x224 + GPS/compass + goal category (+ previous action)
setting.action_space: discrete STOP / MOVE_FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN_LEFT / TURN_RIGHT 30° / LOOK_UP / LOOK_DOWN (LoCoBot embodiment)

numbers_note: All episode sets are regenerated by the authors for 6 goal categories (bed, chair, sofa, tv, plant, toilet) and are not the official Habitat challenge episodes, so absolute numbers are not directly comparable to standard HM3D/MP3D ObjectNav leaderboards. HSSD-60 numbers come from data labels printed in Figure 6. Figure 6 also shows two unexplained ProcTHOR points near 5K–10K scenes (e.g. 11.6/12.5 SR on HM3DSem). Section 6 text reports HSSD-122 zero-shot MP3D as 12.56% SR / 4.56 SPL, while Table 5 and a later paragraph give 14.44 / 5.17; Table 5 values are used here. Standard errors over 3 runs are in Table 5 but omitted from the metric dicts. Other own-variant results in Table 6 (e.g. HSSD-60 fine-tuned 48.13/22.76) are omitted.
results: Trained on only 122 HSSD scenes, the RL ObjectNav agent reaches 19.15 SR / 7.71 SPL zero-shot on HM3DSem val. The ProcTHOR-10K-trained agent gets 12.53 / 5.26, and the scale-matched ProcTHOR-122 agent gets 9.33 / 3.47. On MP3D val the HSSD agent reaches 14.44 / 5.17, against 8.26 / 2.96 for ProcTHOR-10K. After fine-tuning on HM3DSem, all pretraining sources converge to about 48 SR; HSSD-122 keeps a slight SPL edge (23.10 vs 21.80 for ProcTHOR-10K), and the HM3DSem-only agent gets 48.10 / 22.16.
limitations: Only one agent family is studied (end-to-end pixels-to-actions RL with a frozen CLIP encoder). Modular, map-based and imitation-learning agents are not tested.
Evaluation uses custom 6-category episode sets rather than official challenge splits. Absolute zero-shot performance stays low (19 SR on HM3DSem vs 48 when trained in-domain).
Visual realism is bounded by Habitat's rasterization renderer. HSSD is still small (211 scenes), and HSSD-trained agents transfer poorly to THOR-style scenes.
